advances: An affine-cost selector identity for original mixed depth, with no cap coverage assertion.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The actual sampled fibers form a finite compatible family, so 1ec728c26c11b368 gives continuity of $D$ on each. On a positive fiber the ordinary closed halfspace volumes through a point are jointly continuous in the point and the unit normal by dominated convergence off the limiting hyperplane. Taking the minimum over the compact sphere gives ordinary depth continuity. On a null fiber $F=0$, so $D$ and $F$ are continuous on the compact finite union $S$. The compact active set is nonempty and the largest active slope is attained. For base costs the term $b\cdot p$ is constant on a fiber. By 55a57b1cf55d0c87 a boundary mark of a positive fiber has $D=0$, and it has $F=0$ by a supporting ordinary cap. Any interior mark has positive raw own depth and positive mixed depth, so improves the objective within that fiber, including for $\lambda=0$.

Use optimality of $Y_0$ at $\theta_0$ against $Y_1$ and optimality of $Y_1$ at $\theta_1$ against $Y_0$. Rearranging yields the two bounds on $A$, whose difference gives the nonnegative vector exchange. Along the path the objective line of a source has intercept $D(Y)+\theta_0\cdot w(Y)$ and slope $v\cdot w(Y)$. Write $R(t)=D(Y_t)+\theta_0\cdot w(Y_t)$, which is uniquely determined by $E(\theta(t))-tG(t)$. For $s<t$, the same comparisons give
$$
s[G(t)-G(s)]\le R(s)-R(t)\le t[G(t)-G(s)].
$$
Thus $G$ is nondecreasing and bounded by compactness. The envelope is Lipschitz along the path since all slopes are bounded. For $t_j\downarrow t$ from the right, a subsequence of active $Y_{t_j}$ converges to a source active at $t$ by continuity. Its slope is the right limit of $G$ by continuity of $w$ and monotonicity. This limit is at most the largest active slope at $t$, and monotonicity gives the reverse inequality. This proves right continuity.

Sum the two comparison bounds over a partition of $[a,b]$. The intercept drops telescope. The lower and upper sums are those for integration of the identity function against the finite measure with $\mu_G((s,t])=G(t)-G(s)$ on $(a,b]$. Their difference is at most the mesh times $G(b)-G(a)$, which tends to zero. Thus $R(a)-R(b)=\int_{(a,b]}t\,dG(t)$ exactly, including any jump at $b$. Substituting the adjusted intercept yields the claimed actual depth identity. The argument uses only selected endpoint values and does not require a measurable maximizing source path.

statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $n,d\ge1$, with positive summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)$ be its raw closed-halfspace depth and $F(Y)$ the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber of $Y=(z,x)$, using zero on null fibers. Fix either $p(Y)=z$ or $p(Y)=Y$. Put $w(Y)=(F(Y),p(Y))$ and $E(\theta)=\max_{Y\in S}[D(Y)+\theta\cdot w(Y)]$ for $\theta=(\lambda,b)$ with $\lambda\ge0$. All maxima are attained. Base costs admit only own-interior optimizers within each selected positive fiber. If $Y_i$ is active at $\theta_i$ for $i=0,1$, put $\delta w=w(Y_1)-w(Y_0)$ and $A=D(Y_0)-D(Y_1)$. Then
$$
\theta_0\cdot\delta w\le A\le\theta_1\cdot\delta w,\qquad
(\theta_1-\theta_0)\cdot\delta w\ge0.
$$
Along a feasible affine path $\theta(t)=\theta_0+t v$, select any active $Y_t$ of largest slope $G(t)=v\cdot w(Y_t)$. The largest slope is bounded, nondecreasing and right-continuous wherever the path has a right neighborhood. For every finite interval $[a,b]$ of feasible parameters,
$$
D(Y_a)-D(Y_b)=\int_{(a,b]}t\,dG(t)+\theta_0\cdot[w(Y_b)-w(Y_a)].
$$
The integral uses the right-continuous Lebesgue–Stieltjes convention.
